brief.subject: Pittsburgh eyes 2% tax on investment and rental income
brief.headline: Pittsburgh Proposal Would Tax Investment and Rental Income at 2%
brief.dek: A Pittsburgh tax plan targets dividends and rents, trucking clients face IFTA record rules, and big installment sales carry an interest charge.
brief.lede: A Pittsburgh council member has proposed a 2% tax on unearned income such as dividends, royalties, property sales and some rental profits.

sections.heading: Pittsburgh Floats New 2% Tax
bullets: Councilwoman Barb Warwick introduced a bill adding a 2% levy on dividends, royalties and property sale proceeds.
Some rental property income could also be taxed, a concern for local landlords and real estate investors.
The proposal comes as the city faces a dire financial outlook, so the debate may move quickly.

sections.heading: Trucking Clients: Keep IFTA Records
bullets: The IFTA Procedures Manual requires licensees to keep the distance and fuel records behind each return for four years.
Missing mileage or fuel logs can leave carriers exposed if a fuel tax audit arrives.
Bookkeepers serving trucking firms should confirm those records are complete and retrievable now.

sections.heading: Big Installment Sales Carry a Cost
bullets: Once a seller's installment obligations for the year exceed $5 million, Section 453A adds an annual interest charge on deferred tax.
Owners selling a business on installment terms should model that charge before closing the deal.

sections.heading: IRS Regulatory Watch
bullets: The IRS partially withdrew proposed Section 355 rules on the device test and active trade or business requirement.
Those rules govern tax-free spin-offs of controlled corporation stock, affecting corporations and their shareholders.
The IRS Advisory Council has announced a public meeting, per a Federal Register notice.

brief.seo_description: Pittsburgh weighs a 2% tax on dividends and rents, IFTA's four-year record rule, the $5 million installment sale threshold, and IRS updates.
